arxiv-2104-01932.title: The Phosphine Controversy: Is it Phosphine? Is there life on Venus?
arxiv-2104-01932.creator: Priya Hasan
arxiv-2104-01932.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Priya Hasan. On 14th September 2020, the Royal Astronomical Society made an official statement coupled with a webminar on the discovery of phosphine on Venus. Single-line millimetre-waveband spectral detections of phosphine (with a signal-to-noise ratio of ≈ \approx 15 σ \sigma ) from the JCMT and ALMA telescopes indicated a phosphine abundance of 20 ppb 1 1 1 ppb: parts per billion , 1000 times more than that on the Earth.

arxiv-2104-06818.title: Particle beam eigen-emittances, phase integral, vorticity, and rotations
arxiv-2104-06818.creator: L. Groening and C. Xiao, M. Chung
arxiv-2104-06818.description: Abstract Particle beam eigen-emittances comprise the lowest set of rms-emittances that can be imposed to a beam through symplectic optical elements. For cases of practical relevance this paper introduces an approximation providing a very simple and powerful relation between transverse eigen-emittance variation and the beam phase integral. This relation enormously facilitates modeling eigen-emittance tailoring scenarios.

arxiv-2309-15839.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Utkarsh Dwivedi, Salma Elsayed-Ali, Elizabeth Bonsignore & Hernisa Kacorri. Understanding how children design and what they value in AI interfaces that allow them to explicitly train their models such as teachable machines, could help increase such activities’ impact and guide the design of future technologies. In a co-design session using a modified storyboard, a team of 5 children (aged 7-13 years) and adult co-designers, engaged in AI problem formulation activities where they imagine their own teachable machines.

arxiv-2501-19114.description: Abstract Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is a commonly used tool for dimension reduction and denoising. Therefore, it is also widely used on the data prior to training a neural network. However, this approach can complicate the explanation of explainable AI (XAI) methods for the decision of the model.

arxiv-2505-19068.title: Recalibrating binary probabilistic classifiers
arxiv-2505-19068.creator: Dirk Tasche
arxiv-2505-19068.description: Abstract Recalibration of binary probabilistic classifiers to a target prior probability is an important task in areas like credit risk management. We analyse methods for recalibration from a distribution shift perspective. Distribution shift assumptions linked to the area under the curve (AUC) of a probabilistic classifier are found to be useful for the design of meaningful recalibration methods.

arxiv-2508-20609.title: Representative Random Sampling of Chemical Space
arxiv-2508-20609.creator: Diego J. Monterrubio-Chanca, Guido Falk von Rudorff
arxiv-2508-20609.description: Abstract The overwhelming majority of molecules remains unexplored. This is mostly due to the sheer number of them, which prohibits any enumeration of chemical space, the set of all such molecules. In practice, only subsets of chemical space are considered, but those subsets exhibit substantial bias, prohibiting data-driven characterization of chemical space itself.

pmc-10721448.creator: Toshiki Kuno, Kyohei Yamaji, Tadao Aikawa, Mitsuaki Sawano, Tomo Ando, Yohei Numasawa, Hideki Wada, Tetsuya Amano, Ken Kozuma, Shun Kohsaka
pmc-10721448.description: AimsTransradial intervention (TRI) for percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is used to reduce periprocedural complications. However, its effectiveness and safety for patients on dialysis are not well established. We aimed to investigate the association of TRI with in-hospital complications in dialysis patients undergoing PCI.

pmc-11712201.title: Relationships Between NIH Toolbox Cognitive Battery Subtests and In Vivo Amyloid and Tau in People with Amnestic Mild Cognitive Impairment and Dementia of the Alzheimer’s Type
pmc-11712201.creator: Joshua T Fox‐Fuller, Kenneth Petscavage, Ginny Rogers, Robert A. Koeppe, Roger L. Albin, Alexandru D Iordan, Benjamin M. Hampstead, Annalise Rahman‐Filipiak
pmc-11712201.description: BackgroundThe computerized NIH Toolbox Cognition Battery (NIHTB‐CB) was designed to assess cognitive functioning across the lifespan. Previous studies demonstrated that NIHTB‐CB measures discriminate between healthy controls (HCs), individuals with amnestic mild cognitive impairment (aMCI), and individuals with dementia of the Alzheimer’s type (DAT). Scores on NIHTB‐CB tasks also correspond with performance on well‐validated neuropsychological measures of the same cognitive domains.

pmc-12382180.title: Anticancer effects of folic acid-functionalized covalent organic framework containing doxorubicin on SW480 colon cancer cells: a promising tool for drug targeted delivery
pmc-12382180.creator: Razie Ezati, Behrooz Johari, Jaber Yousefi Seyf, Yousef Mortazavi, Mehdi Azizi, Hadi Samadian
pmc-12382180.description: Colorectal cancer is one of the deadliest forms of gastrointestinal cancer, with conventional treatments often facing significant limitations. As a result, new approaches, particularly in targeted drug delivery, have shown great promise. In this study, the COF-FA@DOX nanocarrier was developed, where covalent organic frameworks (COFs) were functionalized with folic acid (FA) and then loaded with Doxorubicin (DOX).

pmc-12722775.creator: Sukyung Kim, Inbo Oh, Jaeyoung Choi, Jihyun Kim, Jiwon Kim, Jin-Hee Bang, Young-Min Kim, Kangmo Ahn
pmc-12722775.description: BackgroundStudies that examine a link between long-term exposure to ambient particulate matter (PM) and atopic dermatitis (AD) in children are lacking. This longitudinal study aimed to investigate the effect of long-term exposure to PM on AD in infants.MethodsWe enrolled 150 infants aged 0–1 years with AD and followed them until age 3 in Seoul, Korea.

pmc-13163483.title: Opioid Signaling in Multiple Sclerosis: Emerging Targets for Repair
pmc-13163483.creator: Renata Perlikowska, Małgorzata Domowicz, Agnieszka Śliwińska, Mariusz Stasiołek
pmc-13163483.description: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic immune-mediated disorder of the central nervous system (CNS) characterized by persistent inflammation, demyelination, and progressive neurodegeneration, driven largely by aberrant activation of T and B lymphocytes that infiltrate the CNS and cause myelin and axonal damage, leading to neurological impairment.

pmc-13182921.title: Comparative genomics reveals high prophage diversity and horizontal gene transfer of effectors and phage defence systems in the Pseudomonas syringae complex
pmc-13182921.creator: Dominique Holtappels, George E.J. Rickus, Túlio Morgan, Rafael R. de Rezende, Britt Koskella, Poliane Alfenas-Zerbini
pmc-13182921.description: The mobilome, defined as the collection of mobile genetic elements within a bacterial genome, plays a role in the adaptation of bacteria to abiotic and biotic drivers. In particular, prophages have been reported to contribute to bacterial resistance to virulent bacteriophages, to competitive interactions among bacterial hosts within microbial communities and to pathogenicity and virulence.

pmc-13187045.title: MFR-YOLO: advancing UAV object detection with multi-scale feature refinement via deformable convolution and global attention
pmc-13187045.creator: Jiaxiang Ge, Huangming Lv, Yaoxuan Guo, Yao Chen, Yuchen Xu, Xuekun Yang
pmc-13187045.description: Unmanned aerial vehicle imagery exhibits extreme scale variance, high small-object density, and arbitrary geometric distortions, which continue to pose challenges to the state-of-the-art detectors like YOLO series. This paper proposes MFR-YOLO, an enhanced model built upon a multi-scale feature refinement network.

pmc-13488216.creator: Yao Liu, Jing Guo, Yiwen Tan, Yingyuan Wang, Xiying Xiang, Juan Du, Wenqing Kang, Mingyan Hei
pmc-13488216.description: BackgroundCongenital heart disease (CHD) may cause intestinal hypoperfusion and feeding intolerance. Neonates who underwent abdominal surgery were subdivided into two groups: those with CHD and those without.

pmc-13558360.title: Revisiting chemical kinetics for H + CH4 → H2 + CH3 using variational transition state theory: comparison with global dynamics calculations
pmc-13558360.creator: Edson F. V. de Carvalho, Marcelo A. P. Pontes, Luiz F. A. Ferrão, Francisco B. C. Machado, Orlando Roberto-Neto
pmc-13558360.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ContextFor both the forward and reverse reaction, there are no accurate rate constants at the VTST/MT level using potential energy surfaces built with the density functional theory (DFT) approach. Calculations of rate constants in function of temperature are carried out for the elementary reaction H + CH4 → H2 + CH3 using variational transition state theory with multidimensional tunneling corrections (VTST/MT) with density functional theory (DFT) and are compared with previous global dynamics calculations reported in the literature.
